answer: Latency-History Admission Threshold. Each identity must sustain a minimum age of organic request timing before its actions count: inter-arrival gaps must match a server-issued quartz clock profile, so traffic arriving at machine speed or at the burst zenith of a fresh cohort is throttled to zero weight. The rule enforces a rolling 30-day timing history, and any identity whose gaps cluster fails admission until it accrues real variance. An attacker pays 30 days of wall-clock time per identity plus the bandwidth to emulate plausible jitter; no fable of instant scale survives it.
